subject: SIG: Hosting scenario playbook — ownership, dataflows, and evidence mapping
messages:
From: Acme Security <security@acme.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-12T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: SIG questionnaire - clarifying hosting modes and evidence needed

Hi Vivek,

Thanks for taking this — attached is our SIG starter (acme-sig-starter.xlsx). Our InfoSec team needs a concise mapping of responsibilities and evidence for the three Redwood hosting models: Hosted API, Dedicated (reserved capacity), and Private (VPC/on-prem). In particular:

- Who (Redwood vs customer) is responsible for data at rest/encryption, key management (KMS/HSM) and logs in each mode?
- Network boundary diagrams (where in-path traffic traverses ACME networks vs Redwood) for each mode.
- Evidence artifacts we can upload to our intake (SOC2 scope, encryption config screenshots, deployment tenancy proof).
- Any operational fallbacks (e.g., automatic routing to Hosted when Dedicated is constrained) and how customer consent/controls are enforced.

Can you provide a short playbook and attach any diagrams or artifacts (pdf/png) that we can pass to our auditors? If possible, please answer inline in the attached starter spreadsheet. Let me know if you need a short call.

Cheers,
Asha Patel
Acme Security Team

Attachment: acme-sig-starter.xlsx

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Asha Patel <security@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-12T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SIG questionnaire - clarifying hosting modes and evidence needed

Hi Asha — thanks for the clear ask. I put together a short playbook below and attached two artifacts that should help your auditors: hosting-playbook-v1.pdf (narrative + responsibility matrix) and network-diagram-hosted-dedicated.png (high-level flow). I've also started filling the starter spreadsheet with pointers — see the attached acme-sig-starter.xlsx you sent with comments.

Executive summary (short):
- Hosted API: Redwood handles runtime, key storage (customer-managed KMS optional for enterprise), tokenization, and SOC2-covered storage for logs/metrics within our multi-tenant environment. Customers are responsible for their prompt/content classification and end-user consent. Evidence: SOC2 report excerpt (scoped controls), encryption-at-rest config, sample audit log extract.

- Dedicated (reserved capacity): Dedicated GPU pools logically isolated per customer. Data plane is isolated (separate containers/namespaces and optional VPC peering). Customer controls KMS keys for model artifacts and optional PII redaction hooks. Evidence: tenant allocation screenshot, VPC peer config, SOC2 + dedicated deployment checklist. Note: Failover policy can route to compatible dedicated pools first; fallback to Hosted or another region is controlled by the customer's org policy (we do not unilaterally switch to a different tenant).

- Private (VPC / on-prem): Full private control plane provisioned into the customer's VPC or on-prem air-gapped bundle. Customer is owner of network, KMS/HSM, and persistent storage. Redwood provides the operator bundle, documentation, and an optional managed-support contract. Evidence: deployment manifest, attestations for HSM integration, install logs.

Key technical notes (high level):
- Encryption: TLS in transit (mTLS for Dedicated/Private); AES-256 (or equivalent) at rest. Customers may supply keys via KMS/HSM integrations (supported in Dedicated and Private; Hosted supports customer-supplied KMS via enterprise enrollment).
- Audit logs: Token-level tracing stored per tenant; retention and export configured per contract. For Hosted we provide filtered exports; for Dedicated/Private, full raw logs can be exported to customer storage.
- Routing & fallback: Smart routing layer respects customer routing policy (by default prefer Dedicated region/pool); automatic fallback requires explicit agreement/rollout config in the customer's account.

Next steps / asks for your team:
1) Upload the starter spreadsheet back with columns: desired evidence artifacts, priority level, and redaction needs.
2) If you require KMS Customer Key Management in Hosted, note that under "Dedicated/Private preference" so we can surface the enterprise enrollment path.
3) If you want an architecture workshop, Marissa can run a 45-minute deep-dive (technical) and we can capture diagrams for your intake.

I'll leave Marissa and Lauren to add the technical artifacts and internal references below.

Thanks,
Vivek
Head of Product Partnerships | Redwood Inference

Attachments: hosting-playbook-v1.pdf, network-diagram-hosted-dedicated.png

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Asha Patel <security@acme.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-12T14:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SIG questionnaire - clarifying hosting modes and evidence needed

Asha / team — quick technical clarifications to support the playbook above. I'm pasting the short evidence checklist you can link into the spreadsheet and our internal doc links.

Hosted API evidence (what we can provide immediately):
- SOC2 Type II report excerpt (control IDs called out for key management and data handling) — redacted copy.
- Sample encryption config screen (Hosted console) showing AES-256 enabled.
- Sample audit log extract (7 days) with token-level latency metrics (PII redacted).
- Diagram: single-tenant logical overlay on multi-tenant runtime (see attached PNG).

Dedicated evidence (what we can provide):
- Tenant allocation (DB/container) snapshot and allocation ticket.
- Network peer configuration example (VPC peering template).
- KMS integration proof (KMS key ARN plus short audit trace of key usage).
- Operational checklist showing autoscale and burst policies (for lead times).

Private evidence (on-prem / VPC):
- Deployment manifest and versioned operator bundle hash (we provide the hash and signed manifest).
- HSM attestation summary (if customer configures HSM).
- Install logs with manifests and service startup timestamps.

Notes on isolation and KV cache: in Dedicated and Private modes KV cache is provisioned per tenant; keys do not cross-tenant boundaries. For Hosted, we use prefix-based namespace isolation and strict runtime fencing with nightly reconciliation jobs. If you need a deeper forensic proof, we can run a forensic snapshot in a non-prod window for validation.

Drive links (internal):
- hosting playbook: https://drive.google.com/open?id=hosting-playbook-v1
- internal evidence index: https://redwood.internal/docs/sig-hosting-playbook

If you mark any artifact as "elevated" in the spreadsheet (requires exec sign-off), we'll put that on the next compliance sprint.

—Marissa
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Acme Security <security@acme.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-13T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SIG questionnaire - clarifying hosting modes and evidence needed

Vivek / Marissa — thanks, this is very helpful. A few follow ups after reviewing the attachments:

- Can you confirm the Dedicated fallback behavior: if a customer's Dedicated pool hits capacity and the org routing policy allows fallback, will calls ever be routed into a multi-tenant Hosted runtime that could mix workloads? We need language for our risk register.
- We'd like a short artifact demonstrating KV-cache tenant separation in Dedicated (screenshot or signed note).
- For Hosted where customer-supplied KMS is requested, please confirm the timeline and whether any secret material is ever stored on Redwood-managed keystores.

I've uploaded our completed matrix with target evidence columns as acme-sig-matrix.xlsx. If possible, can Marissa run the 45-minute technical workshop next week (we prefer Tue/Wed morning PST)?

Cheers,
Asha
Acme Security Team

Attachment: acme-sig-matrix.xlsx
